What tranches are published, what they cost, and what changed

Source: R/md-tranche-tools.R
md_tranches.Rd

md_tranches() lists the files in a tranche build: table, layer, class, rows, size, and whether each is already here. Given a spec, it marks the files md_compile() needs for it and totals what md_fetch_tranches() would still have to download. md_tranche_manifest() returns the build's whole manifest: the build id, when and from which commit it was built, the normalizer signature, the database fingerprint and the file list. md_tranche_diff() compares two builds file by file, which is what a user needs before updating: which files changed, how many rows each gained or lost, and whether the normalizer changed. md_tranches_prune() deletes the parquet files of builds no longer in use, keeping their manifests as the record of what was once here.

Usage

md_tranches(
  spec = NULL,
  build = NULL,
  remote = md_remote(),
  root = md_path("tranches"),
  local = FALSE
)

md_tranche_manifest(
  build = NULL,
  remote = md_remote(),
  root = md_path("tranches"),
  local = FALSE
)

md_tranche_diff(
  old,
  new = NULL,
  remote = md_remote(),
  root = md_path("tranches")
)

md_tranches_prune(keep = 1L, root = md_path("tranches"))

Arguments

spec

An md_spec(): mark and total the files it needs.

build

A build id; by default the newest one (latest.json).

remote

The base URL of a matchdb copy.

root

The local tranche directory.

local

Read the local copy of the manifest instead of the remote one.

old, new

Builds to compare: build ids (read from the local copies when here, else from the remote) or manifests from md_tranche_manifest(). new defaults to the newest published build.

keep

How many builds to keep whole, newest first. The build latest.json names is always kept.

Value

md_tranches(): a data frame of class md_tranches, one row per file: table, layer, variant_class, rows, mb, here and, given a spec, needed. The manifest's build fields ride along as attributes.

md_tranche_manifest(): the manifest as a list; files is a data frame with path, table, layer, variant_class, rows, bytes, md5.

md_tranche_diff(): a data frame of class md_tranche_diff, one row per file in either build: status (same, changed, added, removed), rows_old, rows_new, mb_new. The two builds' fields are attributes old and new.

md_tranches_prune(): the bytes freed, invisibly.

Updating

A new build is a new folder; nothing in an old one is overwritten. Rows are not layered in: the derived columns, statistics cells, clusters and compact tables are rebuilt over the whole database for every build, so a new release changes files whose source rows did not change. What can be saved is the download: md_fetch_tranches() copies any file whose md5 matches one already in an older local build instead of downloading it again, and md_tranche_diff() says how much that will be beforehand.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
md_tranches()                                   # everything in the newest build
md_tranches(md_spec(layers = "bmf_active"))     # what one spec would download
md_tranche_manifest()$normalize_signature
md_tranche_diff("2026-10-27-82c6f0cb")          # that build against the newest
} # }
